text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's interim Prime minister Stefan Sofianski leaves on Tuesday for Germany to inform 20 major investors on privatisation plans for 22 Bulgarian state-owned firms, including Balkan Airlines, Neftochim oil refinery, steel works and shipyards.
Sofianski is to be joined on Wednesday by Ivan Kostov, the leader of the Union of Democratic Forces who is expected to form the new government.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet appointed Bozhidar Kabakchiev as Bulgaria's representative at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in the place of Kalin Mitrev. Kabakchiev was an executive director of Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency from November 1994 to March 1995.
-- Bulgaria's second biggest Plama oil refinery said it has been operating at one third of its capacity while it awaits permission to import crude through the Black Sea port of Bourgas.
-- Bulgaria hopes to reschedule $50 million of payments on its debt to the Paris club of government creditors due this year, a government official said.

-- Bulgaria's interim government has prepared a draft bill to restructure the Bulgarian National Bank ahead of planned introduction of a fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board system, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.
-- Switzerland's Surito Investments AG was interested in buying a stake in Bulgaria's First Private Bank, which was put in receivership by the central bank last year, visiting Surito officials said.
-- Bulgaria's National Electricity Company (NEC) said it would curb supplies to some of its industrial clients who had not paid their bills. Debtor firms owe some 61 billion levs to NEC.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov appointed Vasilii Takev as Bulgaria's ambassador in Russia. Takev was Bulgaria's ambassador in Argentina and Paraguay.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet said it would propose to parliament a scheme for unblocking some 9.6 million Ecus extended to the country under the EU's PHARE programme and blocked in three Bulgarian banks when the banks were put in receivership last year.

-- A mission of the International Monetary Fund lead by Anne McGuirk is expected to arrive in Sofia today for talks with the interim cabinet on Bulgaria's 1997 budget draft and the preparations for implementation of a fixed rate exchange regime. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
